subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Bald Eagle's Comeback
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Bald Eagle's Comeback.

hook.text: By 1963, only 417 breeding pairs of bald eagles remained in the lower 48 US states.

buildup.text: DDT pesticide thinned their eggshells so badly that eggs broke during incubation.

discovery.text: The US banned DDT in 1972 and listed eagles under the Endangered Species Act.

twist.text: Captive breeding programs and habitat protection slowly rebuilt the population.

climax.text: By 2020, over 71,000 breeding pairs were counted. The eagle was removed from the endangered list.

punchline.text: A nation's symbol was saved by the laws that nation wrote.

quiz.question: What caused the bald eagle population to crash?

details.summary: Bald eagles were driven to near extinction in the lower 48 states by DDT-induced eggshell thinning, habitat loss, and hunting. After DDT was banned in 1972 and the species was placed on the Endangered Species List, populations recovered from 417 to over 300,000 breeding pairs.
details.whyItMatters: The bald eagle's recovery is one of conservation's greatest success stories. It proves that strong regulation and species protection work when applied consistently.
takeaways: DDT thinned eagle eggshells, causing reproductive failure
The 1972 DDT ban and Endangered Species Act drove recovery
Eagle numbers grew from 417 pairs in 1963 to over 300,000 today

faq.question: How did DDT nearly wipe out bald eagles?
faq.answer: DDT accumulated in the food chain and concentrated in fish-eating birds like eagles. The chemical caused eggshells to thin so severely that they broke during incubation. By 1963 only 417 nesting pairs remained in the contiguous United States.

faq.question: How long did it take for bald eagle populations to recover?
faq.answer: Recovery took roughly 35 years of concerted effort. DDT was banned in 1972, eagles were listed under the Endangered Species Act in 1978, and by 2007 populations had recovered enough to be delisted. Numbers continue to grow.
